question: In a burn wound, what is the central area called where the maximum tissue damage happens?
explanation: Think of the zone of coagulation as ground zero—it's closest to the heat, so the cells are completely destroyed and can't recover. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

options.A: It represents the maximum depth of permanent skin and muscle destruction.
options.B: Infection rarely occurs in this specific layer of the burn wound.
options.C: This area is completely insensate and requires immediate surgical removal.
options.D: Tissue in this zone has reduced blood flow and can be saved from necrosis.

explanation: The zone of stasis is bruised and sluggish, but not dead yet! Quick fluids keep blood flowing there so it doesn't cross over into tissue death (necrosis). Great nursing care saves the day! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h1)

question: Using the Rule of Nines, what percentage of the total body surface area does an adult's entire front chest and abdomen (anterior trunk) cover?
explanation: The Rule of Nines is a classic! The front trunk is 18 percent, and the back trunk is also 18 percent. Easy points for your exams! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h2)

question: A patient has a burn that looks leathery, dry, and white, and they feel no pain when it's touched. How would you chart this?
explanation: When all skin layers and nerve endings are fried, it's a full-thickness burn. That's why it looks leathery and doesn't hurt to touch—the nerves are gone! You're building great clinical eyes. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main reason burn shock happens within the first 24 hours of a severe burn?

options.A: Complete cessation of red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.B: Sudden slowing of the heart rate due to vagal nerve stimulation
options.C: Massive fluid shift from blood vessels into body tissues
options.D: Rapid drop in core body temperature from environmental exposure

explanation: Right after a big burn, leaky blood vessels let plasma rush out into the tissues. This sudden fluid loss causes burn shock, which is why aggressive fluid replacement is priority number one! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which lab result is a classic sign right after a patient suffers a major burn and goes into shock?

options.C: Elevated platelet count from bone marrow failure
options.D: Elevated hematocrit due to fluid loss

explanation: Since the liquid part of the blood (plasma) leaks out into the body, what's left behind is thick blood! This makes the hematocrit shoot up until IV fluids balance things out. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when helping someone with a fresh thermal burn?

options.A: Apply antibiotic ointment to prevent infection
options.B: Apply ice packs directly to the wound to reduce swelling
options.C: Stop the burning process and apply cool water
options.D: Scrub the burn vigorously with antiseptic soap

explanation: Always stop the burning first and cool it with clean running water! Never use ice, though—it causes blood vessels to clamp down and makes the injury worse. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: A patient arrives with burnt nose hairs, blackish sputum, and a very hoarse voice. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Apply silver sulfadiazine cream to the face
options.B: Calculate the exact total body surface area percentage
options.C: Administer oral analgesics for pain control

explanation: Those are classic signs of smoke inhalation! The airway can swell shut very quickly, so getting ready to tube the patient is a true lifesaver. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which IV fluid is the gold standard for fluid resuscitation during the first day of major burn care?
explanation: Lactated Ringer's is closest in makeup to our body's own blood plasma, making it the top choice for refilling those empty tanks after a burn. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h5)

question: An adult weighing 70 kg has a 40 percent burn and is getting IV fluids. What hourly urine output tells you their organs are getting enough blood flow?
explanation: We aim for 0.5 to 1 mL per kg per hour for adults. For a 70 kg patient, that's 35 to 70 mL/hr. Urine output is our best cheat code to know if fluid resuscitation is working! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h5)

question: What kind of skin graft uses skin taken from another part of the patient's own body?
explanation: Auto means self! An autograft uses the patient's own skin so their body won't reject it. Smart healing science! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why do modern burn teams rush to surgically remove dead burn tissue (eschar) early on?

options.A: It removes dead tissue that serves as a breeding ground for infection.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent skin grafting procedures.
options.C: It immediately restores full sensory nerve function to the area.
options.D: It prevents the systemic release of inflammatory cytokines forever.

explanation: Dead skin (eschar) is like a feast for bacteria. Getting rid of it early stops severe infections and gets the wound ready for a healthy graft. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the preferred way to feed a patient with a major burn injury?

options.A: Total parenteral nutrition through a central line
options.C: Strict oral diet supplemented only by clear fluids
options.D: Intravenous amino acid infusions without lipids

explanation: Feed the gut if it works! Early tube feeding keeps the stomach lining strong, stops bacteria from leaking, and fuels their massive healing needs. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why do major burn survivors need a massive amount of protein in their diet while recovering?

options.A: To offset massive protein catabolism and support wound healing
options.B: To maintain normal blood pressure by increasing plasma volume
options.C: To prevent the development of permanent metabolic acidosis
options.D: To suppress the inflammatory immune response completely

explanation: Major burns put the body into overdrive, burning through muscle and protein super fast. High protein intake feeds the repair process so new tissue can grow. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?
explanation: Think 'Curling' up from belly pain after a burn! It's a classic stress ulcer caused by low blood flow to the stomach early in shock. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)

question: Which sign tells you a limb with a tight, wrapping (circumferential) burn is developing compartment syndrome?

options.A: Sudden appearance of localized skin blisters
options.B: Hyperactive bowel sounds and abdominal pain
options.C: Elevated core body temperature and chills
options.D: Loss of distal pulses and capillary refill

explanation: As a circumferential burn swells, it acts like a tourniquet, cutting off circulation inside. Losing pulse and slow refill means pressure is dangerously high! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of having burn survivors wear custom pressure garments during recovery?

options.A: To prevent the development of deep vein thrombosis
options.B: To protect the fragile skin from ultraviolet sun rays
options.C: To provide continuous warmth to grafted skin areas
options.D: To minimize hypertrophic scarring and flatten keloids

explanation: Constant, gentle pressure helps train healing collagen fibers to lie flat, keeping raised scars and keloids under control over time. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h9)

question: Why are proper body positioning and early splinting so important in burn rehab?

options.A: To prevent debilitating joint contractures caused by scar tightening
options.B: To maintain adequate arterial blood pressure in the extremities
options.C: To speed up the re-epithelialization of superficial donor sites
options.D: To stop the hypermetabolic energy expenditure phase early

explanation: Healing burn scars love to pull and tighten joints into awkward bends. Splints and good positioning keep patients stretched out and moving freely! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h9)
